done.why: I got out of the cliff trouble and was given a staff. I didn't know what to do with it, so I stopped there.

about: A dungeon adventure that starts at the bottom of an endless stair. You are on a last test before meeting an old silver-haired man. I only saw a junction with a sword stuck in a rock, a barren area, and a sunlit cliff with a con man who tricks you out of a chest.

ending.what: No ending. The nearest thing was being hauled up the cliff and given a wooden staff.

moments.note: The dark place and the grue warning made me think I'd done something wrong. I only worked out that the lantern needed turning on.
I said hello and the game answered Goodbye.
I climbed down the rope and then couldn't get back up. I had been warned it was doubtful, but I didn't take that in.
I shouted up and the unseen man answered. It made the place feel alive.
While I waited, the sounds from above changed each time: the lock giving, a whistle, pacing. It built the feeling that I'd been swindled.

wished: I wished I knew what the staff was for.
I wished I could have talked to the figure among the trees.
I wished the game had explained how to light the lantern before I walked into the dark.

lines.line: Who do you think you are? Arthur?
lines.why: A joke that made the world feel playful.

lines.line: From somewhere above you, at the top of the cliff, somebody finds this funny, briefly, and stops.
lines.why: It showed me I was being watched, and it made me uneasy.

fun.why: The cliff scene was fun. The rest was mostly walking around.

engagement.why: The man above kept me curious. The long wait made my interest sag.

difficulty.why: The puzzle resolved with the obvious moves. The only friction was the lantern in the dark and the wording of some commands.

interestingness.why: The sunlit oasis, the hidden watcher, and the con on the cliff were all intriguing.

prose.why: Vivid descriptions, especially the thing among the trees that is a trunk whenever you look straight at it, and the sounds of the unseen man.
